methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Neustark is a Series B climate and energy technology company that has raised $70M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector and adjacent development stages, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $133M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M—produces a median implied valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $113M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $566M. This wide dispersion reflects material stage and maturity differences within the peer set; notably, all three direct comparables are Series C companies, one stage ahead of Neustark. Key uncertainties include technology readiness, capital intensity to commercialization, and the sustainability of frontier-energy valuations in the current environment. The analysis suggests Neustark's fair value most likely lies in the $400M–$700M range, pending clarification on unit economics and path to positive contribution margin.
